A herring gull stands dead centre on the top court, both feet flat, yellow beak aimed at the sea, its full white chest filling the frame above the nearest cut wall face.
A black-headed gull walks the top of the dam one foot precisely in front of the other, dark chocolate head tipped forward, its bright red legs tracking the exact ridge line toward the far end.
An oystercatcher stands on the dam with its right leg folded up flush to its belly, its orange beak a hard vertical against the bright water band, the raised foot still wet.
Three sandpipers run the moat, one ahead and two abreast behind, the leader already rounding the near corner, the last still crossing the far straight, all six legs a blur at sand level.
A herring gull's shadow crosses four turrets in a single unbroken stroke, the wing-tips stretched long across the notched tops, the gull itself small and sharp at the near end of them.
A green shore crab fills the tallest tower's doorway facing outward, its shell the exact width of the arch, both claws forward, sand still damp across its carapace.
A hermit crab hauls its borrowed shell up the outer ramp, the shell's spiral tilted hard left with the effort, leaving a furrowed drag-groove behind it in the wet sand.
A green shore crab sits in the moat bottom with only its eye-stalks clearing the water surface, both claws folded flat, the water above it bright with reflected sky.
A sand-coloured shrimp turns over in a pool caught behind the inner wall, its translucent tail curled and snapping, the grains beneath it spinning in its own small current.
A razor shell stands vertical where something pressed it into the outer wall face, its violet-edged opening level with the top of the near turret, its tip buried two knuckle-lengths down.
A line of dog paw prints runs straight up the ramp and over the crest of the main wall, the far prints already blurring at the edges, the near ones still sharp and deep.
Bird tracks cross and recross the whole top of the dam in a dense pale stitching, older ones pressed flat and faint, fresh ones cutting clean through them at every angle.
A broad drag-trough runs the full length of the outer slope where something heavy was hauled, its twin furrows still wet and dark, a scatter of dislodged grains settling back into them.
Small deep paired prints walk the whole length of the dam and back, the outward set pressed deeper on the left toe, the return set pressed deeper on the right, crossing once at the midpoint.
A green plastic toy soldier stands on the highest turret facing the sea alone, its rifle at its shoulder, its base packed into the notched top so only sand around its boots holds it upright.
Two plastic soldiers, both gone chalky white where the green has worn, are posted at either end of the dam, each facing outward, a full wall's length of open parapet between them.
A small moulded plastic dinosaur, cobalt blue with the paint scoured off its spine ridge, sits on the parapet with the bright water band directly behind its open jaws.
A die-cast digger, its yellow cab paint scoured to bare grey on every raised edge, is parked in the spoil heap at the end of the ramp, its bucket arm lowered into the loose sand.
A chipped plastic knight lies face-down on the ramp, its red plume snapped to a stub, one arm extended downhill, the other pinned under its chest, a furrow in the sand where it slid.
A moulded plastic diver in a faded orange suit stands in the bottom of the moat with the water reaching its chest, its arms at its sides, its helmet just breaking the surface.
A tiny plastic cow, white with black patches, stands on the top court with its four legs square and its head level, the sea band running bright behind it.
A black-headed gull lands hard on the near turret's top, wings still open and forward, tail down, one foot gripping the crest and the other still swinging to find the same edge.
An oystercatcher runs the full length of the outer wall base, its orange beak tucked, its wings pressed tight, its coral-red legs driving fast through the wet skin at the wall's base.
A green shore crab moves sideways along the inner face of the main wall, one claw trailing in the surface of the moat, the other braced against the cut sand above the waterline.
A sandpiper stands dead still in the near corner where the moat meets the dam, one wing half-lifted and not yet folded back down, a single wet grain on the tip of its beak.
